public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Schur's theorem on Galois groups of truncated exponential polynomials

*Reference:* (https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2814220)

*Reference* (https://mathoverflow.net/questions/477077)
-/

@[expose] public section

/-
Note: This was asked by Nick Katz. Quasi-autoformalized using Claude 4.0 Sonnet.
-/

namespace SchurTruncatedExponential

open Polynomial

open scoped Nat

/--
The truncated exponential polynomial `truncatedExp n` is
given by `∑_{j=0}^{n} x^j / j!` over `ℚ`, which is the
`n`-th partial sum of the Taylor series for the exponential function `e^x`.
-/
noncomputable def truncatedExp (n : ℕ) : ℚ[X] :=
  ∑ j ∈ Finset.range (n + 1), (1 / j ! : ℚ) • X ^ j

/--
**Schur's Theorem (1924):**
Let `f_n(x) = ∑_{j=0}^n x^j/j!` be the `n`-th truncated
exponential polynomial over `ℚ`. Then for `n ≥ 2`:

- If `n ≡ 0 (mod 4)`, the Galois group of `f_n` is isomorphic to the alternating group `A_n`
- If `n ≢ 0 (mod 4)`, the Galois group of `f_n` is isomorphic to the symmetric group `S_n`
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12]
theorem schur_truncatedExp_galoisGroup_equiv (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≥ 2) :
  letI f := truncatedExp n
  if n % 4 = 0 then
    -- Galois group is alternating group A_n
    Nonempty (f.Gal ≃* alternatingGroup (Fin n))
  else
    -- Galois group is symmetric group S_n
    Nonempty (f.Gal ≃* Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) := by
  sorry

end SchurTruncatedExponential

findings.description: The docstring at line 49 labels this result “Schur's Theorem (1924)”, but the cited Galois-group classification is attributed to Schur's 1930 paper. This is a historical reference error only; the Lean proposition correctly states the classification.
findings.source_evidence: Robert F. Coleman, “On the Galois Groups of the Exponential Taylor Polynomials”, L'Enseignement Mathématique 33 (1987), p. 183, writes: “In 1930, [S-2], Schur proved the following theorem”, followed by exactly the alternating/symmetric classification in this file. Reference [S-2] on p. 189 is Schur, “Gleichungen ohne Affekt (1930)”. Read through https://www.e-periodica.ch/digbib/ajax/pageinfo?pid=ens-001:1987:33::316 and https://www.e-periodica.ch/digbib/ajax/pageinfo?pid=ens-001:1987:33::322 .
findings.suggested_fix: Change “Schur's Theorem (1924)” to “Schur's Theorem (1930)”; optionally add the reference to “Gleichungen ohne Affekt”.

reformulations.difference: Lean explicitly restricts the classification to n ≥ 2, while the cited theorem is stated for the nth truncated exponential without this lower bound.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The omitted cases are automatic: truncatedExp 0 = 1, whose Galois group and A₀ are both trivial; truncatedExp 1 = 1 + X, whose Galois group and S₁ are both trivial. Consequently the classification for every natural n is equivalent to its restriction to n ≥ 2. This equivalence was proved independently in /workspace/review/scratch.lean as review_domain_equiv, without using the admitted Schur theorem.

review.notes: No mathematical misformalization was found in either declaration. Lean experiments verified the general coefficient formula and natDegree = n, explicit polynomials for n = 0 through 4, nondegenerate branch choices, and the boundary-case equivalence. Mathlib's Polynomial.Gal is the automorphism group of the splitting field over the coefficient field, here ℚ, and the target groups have the intended meanings. The research solved category agrees with the sources. All experiments are in /workspace/review/scratch.lean; the checked coefficient, degree, and equivalence lemmas have no sorryAx dependency.
